Documentation

Grail Docs

Grail is a terminal UI for Gmail, written in Go using Bubble Tea. It lets you read, compose, search, and manage email without leaving your terminal — keyboard-first, no browser required.

This documentation covers everything from installation and OAuth setup to keybindings and configuration. If something is missing or wrong, open an issue on GitHub.

Installation

Grail requires Go 1.21 or later. It runs on Linux, macOS, and WSL2.

Via go install

The fastest way to get started:

shell 
$ go install github.com/Platon223/Grail@latest

Make sure $GOPATH/bin (typically ~/go/bin) is in your $PATH.

Prebuilt binaries

Download a binary for your platform from the GitHub releases page ↗. Extract and place the binary somewhere in your $PATH.

Build from source

shell 
$ git clone https://github.com/Platon223/Grail.git
$ cd Grail
$ go build -o grail .
$ sudo mv grail /usr/local/bin/

Verify the install:

shell 
$ grail --version
grail v0.1.0 (go1.22, linux/amd64)

Authentication

Grail uses Google's official OAuth2 flow with your own Google Cloud Desktop app credentials. Your tokens are stored locally and never sent anywhere outside of Google's APIs.

Before you begin

You need to create a Google Cloud project and download an OAuth2 credentials file. See the OAuth setup guide below if you haven't done this yet.

Once you have your credentials.json file, place it at:

path
~/.config/grail/credentials.json

Then run the auth command:

shell 
$ grail auth
Opening browser for OAuth consent...
If the browser did not open, visit:
  https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth?...
Waiting for authorization...
✓ Authenticated as you@gmail.com
✓ Token saved to ~/.config/grail/token.json

The token is saved to ~/.config/grail/token.json and is automatically refreshed. You only need to run grail auth once per account.

Note

To revoke access at any time, visit myaccount.google.com/permissions ↗ or delete ~/.config/grail/token.json.

Quick start

Once authenticated, you're ready to go:

shell 
$ grail inbox          # open inbox
$ grail inbox --label SENT  # open sent mail
$ grail compose         # new email
$ grail search "from:boss@company.com"

Inbox

The inbox is Grail's main view. It lists your emails with sender, subject, and timestamp. Unread messages are highlighted.

Inbox keybindings

KeyAction
j / ↓Move down
k / ↑Move up
gJump to top
GJump to bottom
Enter / oOpen selected email
cCompose new email
/Search
dDelete (trash)
eArchive
mMark as read/unread
lApply label
rRefresh inbox
qQuit

Loading a specific label

shell
$ grail inbox --label STARRED
$ grail inbox --label SENT
$ grail inbox --label "My Custom Label"

Reading email

Opening an email renders its content using Glamour — HTML is converted to Markdown and displayed with terminal-friendly styling.

Email view keybindings

KeyAction
j / ↓Scroll down
k / ↑Scroll up
SpacePage down
bPage up
rReply
RReply all
fForward
dDelete
eArchive
yCopy email body to clipboard
Esc / qBack to inbox

Composing & replying

The compose view presents a simple form for To, Subject, and the message body. Tab between fields; when the body is focused, the full textarea is available.

Compose keybindings

KeyAction
TabNext field
Shift+TabPrevious field
Ctrl+SSend email
Ctrl+CCancel / discard
Tip

Set editor in your config to open the body in your preferred $EDITOR instead of the inline textarea. This lets you write with full editor support, including plugins and spell check.

Search

Press / from the inbox to open the search prompt. Grail passes your query directly to the Gmail API, so the full Gmail search syntax ↗ is supported.

Common queries

gmail query syntax
from:boss@company.com          # from a specific sender
to:me subject:invoice            # subject contains "invoice"
is:unread after:2024/01/01      # unread since Jan 2024
has:attachment filename:pdf    # emails with PDF attachments
label:work is:starred             # starred in label "work"
larger:5M                          # over 5MB in size

Labels

Press l on any email to open the label picker. You can apply or remove labels, and create new ones inline.

To list all your Gmail labels:

shell
$ grail labels list

Config file

Grail reads its configuration from ~/.config/grail/config.toml. The file is created automatically on first run with defaults. Edit it to customize behavior.

toml 
# ~/.config/grail/config.toml

[general]
editor    = "nvim"       # editor for compose body
browser   = "xdg-open"  # browser for OAuth / links
page_size = 25          # emails per page in inbox

[keybinds]
open    = "o"
reply   = "r"
delete  = "d"
archive = "e"
search  = "/"

[theme]
style = "dark"    # "dark" | "light" | "auto"

All options

KeyDefaultDescription
general.editor $EDITOR Editor used for compose body. Falls back to $EDITOR env var.
general.browser xdg-open Command used to open URLs (OAuth flow, links in emails).
general.page_size 25 Number of emails to fetch per inbox page.
general.date_format relative relative (e.g. "2h ago") or absolute (e.g. "Jun 9 14:32").
theme.style dark dark, light, or auto (follows terminal background).
theme.glamour_style dark Glamour markdown style for email rendering. See glamour styles ↗.

Keybindings

All keybindings can be overridden in the [keybinds] section of your config. Keys are specified as single characters or named keys.

toml
[keybinds]
# inbox
open    = "enter"
reply   = "r"
compose = "c"
delete  = "d"
archive = "e"
search  = "/"
refresh = "r"
label   = "l"
quit    = "q"
Named keys

Supported named keys: enter, space, backspace, tab, esc, up, down, left, right, pgup, pgdown, home, end. Use ctrl+x notation for control combos.

Theming

Grail uses Lipgloss for styling. The built-in themes are dark, light, and auto. Setting auto detects your terminal's background color and picks the closest theme.

Email bodies are rendered with Glamour. You can change the markdown style with the theme.glamour_style option. Available values include dark, light, dracula, tokyo-night, notty, and more.

CLI reference

CommandDescription
grail inboxOpen the inbox TUI. Accepts --label flag.
grail composeOpen the compose view directly.
grail search <query>Search Gmail and open results in the TUI.
grail authRun the OAuth2 authentication flow.
grail auth revokeDelete the stored token.
grail labels listPrint all Gmail labels to stdout.
grail versionPrint version and build info.
grail help [command]Show help for a command.

Global flags

shell
--config   string   path to config file (default: ~/.config/grail/config.toml)
--account  string   Gmail account to use (for multi-account setups)
--no-color           disable color output
--version            print version and exit
--help               print help and exit

OAuth setup guide

Grail requires you to supply your own Google Cloud OAuth2 credentials. This is a one-time setup and takes about five minutes.

  • Go to console.cloud.google.com ↗ and create a new project (or use an existing one).
  • In the sidebar, go to APIs & Services → Library and enable the Gmail API.
  • Go to APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen. Set type to External, fill in the app name, and add your email as a test user.
  • Go to APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth client ID. Choose Desktop app.
  • Download the JSON file and save it to ~/.config/grail/credentials.json.
  • Run grail auth.
Unverified app warning

Google will show an "unverified app" warning during the first OAuth flow. This is expected — your app is in test mode. Click Advanced → Go to [app] (unsafe) to proceed. This warning only appears while the OAuth consent screen is in test mode.

FAQ

I get "invalid_grant" after a while. What does that mean?

The OAuth token has expired or was revoked. Run grail auth again to re-authenticate. This can happen if you haven't used Grail in a while or changed your Google account password.

I get a 403 scope error when trying to send.

Your token was issued with read-only scope. Delete ~/.config/grail/token.json and run grail auth again to authorize with both gmail.readonly and gmail.send scopes.

Can I use Grail with multiple Gmail accounts?

Multi-account support is on the roadmap. For now, you can work around this by maintaining separate config directories and using the --config flag to switch between them.

HTML emails look wrong.

Grail converts HTML to Markdown using Glamour. Complex HTML layouts may not render perfectly — this is a known limitation of text-based rendering. Plain-text emails always render correctly.

Where are my credentials and tokens stored?

Everything lives in ~/.config/grail/. Nothing is stored outside your machine.
